source_title: Crimson Desert Charting the Unknown DLC Gets a Massive Update
source_excerpt:
Pearl Abyss reveals the full details about the launch update for Crimson Desert , and it's Charting the Unknown DLC, bringing new features and content to the game, as well as even more quality of life improvements. While there has been no shortage of updates for Crimson Desert , the game has received the biggest one yet, thanks in large part to the brand-new premium DLC called Charting the Unknown.
Following the launch of Crimson Desert back in March 2026, Pearl Abyss has impressively kept the game updated nearly on a weekly basis. The studio continued to listen to player feedback, identifying many of the game's weak spots and not only made adjustments to them, but also continued to add new features and content. As such, Crimson Desert is a very different game now than it was at launch , even compiling everything into an Enhanced Edition update that was made free for all players back in September. While that was no doubt a big moment for the game, it has now received one of the biggest updates to date thanks to its newly available DLC.
Update 2.04 is a massive one, encompassing all the new features and content within Crimson Desert Charting the Unknown , but also confirming all the behind the scenes changes and improvements as well. Much of the content has already been shown off in pre-launch trailers and announcements, including being able to explore the massive ocean either by a customizable ship or through underwater mounts and diving suit. Players can also design their own house through an expanded housing system, earn trust with NPC characters, or take on new challenges like the Garden of Trials.
Crimson Desert 's narrative has been a weak spot for many players, and while Pearl Abyss has continued to make adjustments in patches and the Enhanced Edition update, Charting the Unknown adds epilogue quests for Kliff, Oongka, and Damiane. These new quests will give players more perspective on where the protagonists are in the story following the end of the main game. However, there's a catch with these new Crimson Desert quests , as players will only find the new missions in the Journal if they've completed the Journey's End mission from the main story.
Identify the silhouettes before time runs out.
However, the update has plenty of new quality of life improvements packed in as well. For example, Pearl Abyss has made major improvements to the NPC interaction UI, largely in part to Crimson Desert 's new romance options . Players can use new Chat and Gift options, while Interact will perform "ordinary" interactions. There's now a dedicated storage box for insects, Barber Shops can be found in major cities, Life Skill tools like a ladle and frying pan are now viable combat options, and Wagons can now be customized with equipment.
While there's likely been plenty of player excitement around being able to not only captain their own ship, but to also full customize it with some really outlandish-looking parts. However, for many, they were taken by surprise to find out that the biggest and best ships in Crimson Desert cost players about 6 million in camp funds, with even more required for additional customized parts. Still, there are options for people who may not have that type of budget as a "Humble Rowboat" will only set players back 2,000 Camp Funds, and even the Small Hernandian Ship comes in at 40k. Either way, the sheer cost of these ships and their customization options have already caused the community to band together to figure out some of the best ways to earn money fast.
Crimson Desert Update 2.04 Release Notes
One individual quest each has been added for Kliff, Oongka, and Damiane. The new quests can be found from the "Journal" menu, after completing "Journey's End" from the main story.
The new quests can be found from the "Journal" menu, after completing "Journey's End" from the main story.
The ocean is now yours to explore. Added a new quest, "A Wider World", that centers around the ocean. The quest will begin after completing "Howling HIll" from the main story and by expanding your Greymane camp above a certain level. Added a gauge for your breath, allowing you to dive underwater. The higher your breath capacity, the longer you can stay underwater. You can increase your maximum breath capacity by refining your diving suit. Added food items that temporarily restores breath. Added equipment that allows the A.T.A.G to operate underwater when equipped. Added "ships" as a new mount. Ships can be constructed through a dispatch mission, or purchased from fleetmasters located throughout Pywel. Ships can also be customized using parts purchased from fleetmasters in Demeniss and Delesyia. You can use your ship for maritime trading, and new trade goods have been added for these trades. Added various new underwater mounts. Depending on their type, underwater mounts can be subdued or fed to increase their Trust. Once their Trust is high enough, they can be resitered as mounts. Added several uncharted islands, which you can pioneer by taking on new missions. Added multiple treasure maps that lets you search for hidden treasures scattered throughout the world.
